flashcards.front: What does the blind king ask Sanjaya in verse 1.1?
flashcards.back: What his sons and the Pandavas did on the battlefield before the war began.

flashcards.front: What did Arjuna ask Krishna, his charioteer, to do?
flashcards.back: Drive his chariot between the two armies so he could see who stood on both sides.
Arjuna's duty was to fight for justice; his love for his relatives pulled the other way. Acknowledge both; dismiss neither.

flashcards.front: Why does facing reality matter here?
flashcards.back: Arjuna saw the people he loved in the opposing army and could not unsee it. Facing a painful truth is the first step to wisdom.
No. Arjuna admitted he did not know what to do instead of pretending to be brave. Doubt is honest, not weak.
Whatever Arjuna chose, someone would suffer. Choose by principle, not by trying to avoid all pain.

flashcards.front: What did Arjuna do instead of deciding alone?
flashcards.back: He turned to Krishna. In life's big questions, seek out wise counsel.
A warrior whose duty was to fight injustice. Know your role and its responsibilities; avoiding duty has consequences too.

flashcards.front: Does compassion mean avoiding hard choices?
flashcards.back: No. Loving those on the other side did not let Arjuna ignore injustice. Kindness does not require abandoning what is right.

flashcards.front: Where does wisdom begin, in this chapter?
flashcards.back: With Arjuna's admission, "I don't know what to do." Humility opened the door to Krishna's teaching.
Arjuna sits down on the back seat of the chariot, his mind overwhelmed with sorrow, and refuses to fight.

quiz.text: Who asks the question that opens the Gita?
quiz.why: In 1.1 the blind king asks Sanjaya what happened on the battlefield.

quiz.text: Why did Arjuna ask for his chariot to go between the armies?

options.B: To see who stood on both sides

quiz.why: He wanted to see the armies on both sides, and there he saw his friends and relatives.

quiz.text: What two forces pull on Arjuna?
quiz.why: Duty to fight for justice against love for his relatives: both are acknowledged.
He admitted he didn't know what to do; doubt is a natural part of life.

quiz.text: If every option causes some suffering, how should one choose?
quiz.why: No choice would please everyone; choose on principle.

quiz.text: Whom does Arjuna turn to when he is lost?

options.B: His guru on the other side

quiz.why: Seeking wisdom from someone wiser, not deciding alone.

quiz.text: "Compassion doesn't mean avoiding hard choices" means:

options.B: Kindness can still do what is right

quiz.why: Loving his relatives did not let Arjuna ignore injustice.

quiz.text: Where does the beginning of wisdom lie, in this chapter?

options.B: In admitting what you don't know

quiz.why: Arjuna's humble admission opens the door to Krishna's teachings.
